 Log in Cubs add backstop Bart off waivers (source)
 17 minutes ago Courtney Hollmon
 Share share-square--:R1qlq: CHICAGO -- The Cubs addressed their catching depth on Friday, claiming Joey Bart off waivers from the White Sox ahead of the 4 p.m. CT non-tender deadline, a source told MLB.com's Mark Feinsand.
 The club has not confirmed the move.

 Bart, 29, is entering his third and final year of arbitration eligibility after being designated for assignment by the White Sox on Tuesday. With Carson Kelly in free agency, the crosstown pickup gives Chicago an experienced Major League backstop to pair with Miguel Amaya while Owen Ayers, who is ranked the club's No. 2 prospect , continues working toward his big league debut. 
 “Bringing in a veteran catcher or someone who's been around [will] certainly mitigate some of the risk of bringing in someone that just hasn't done it before,” Cubs general manager Carter Hawkins told reporters at the General Managers Meetings last week in Las Vegas. “But we got to take risks. We got to take risks to be able to achieve the goals we want to achieve. And we'll be thinking about that and weighing all of that as we make our offseason decisions.”  
 Bart appeared in 44 games across three clubs in 2026, slashing .214/.305/.357 (.662 OPS) with four home runs and 13 RBIs between the Pirates, Braves and White Sox. He played in just three games for the White Sox after being acquired from Atlanta on Aug. 3, fracturing the fifth metacarpal in his left hand on Aug. 6. Though he was activated from the 10-day injured list on Sept. 28, he did not appear in another game. 
 Selected by the Giants with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2018 Draft out of Georgia Tech, Bart rose as high as the No. 14 overall prospect in baseball per MLB Pipeline in 2020. However, he has struggled to find consistency at the big league level, never appearing in more than 97 games in a season while posting a .237/.319/.368 career slash line with 32 home runs and 126 RBIs across 1,107 Major League at-bats.
